request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,
flag, list and line: in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates, the summary, and
any panel added later unless its request says otherwise) is shown as it stood at the end of the last
day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's today was on or before the as-of
date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've built the as-of view and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass on a full `bin/e2e` run (build, start, test, stop).

**How it works**
- **On screen:** the home screen has a date entry, a set button and a clear button, plus a field showing the as-of date (blank when none). The date is kept only in that browser page, so other signed-in users are unaffected. It stays set when the sheet is re-loaded.
- **Requests:** while the date is set, every sheet request from that page carries it in an `X-As-Of` header (added in `core/as-of.interceptor.ts`).
- **Reads:** when the header is present, every read returns the sheet as it stood at the end of that date: the sheet load, people, claims, rates, periods, settings, roles and delegations. Each one is rebuilt from the existing history table using everything changed while the sheet's today was on or before the date. The load also returns the as-of date as the sheet's today, so every figure the screen works out (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, grade and rate in force) uses it. Claim status-log lines after the date are left out.
- **Changes:** a new server check, `history/AsOfGuard.java`, refuses every change that carries the header with a 403 before it reaches its handler, so nothing is written to the store or the audit file. That includes watching a person and the bulk actions, which a viewer may otherwise use. Only the sheet load is let through. Each form shows its usual error element.

**Wider history:** the history table only covered claims, people, rates and dated settings. It now also records periods (including closed and soft-closed), statements, patrons, watches, roles, delegations and the permission matrix. It also records more claim fields (note, opened-by, list order, proofs, split-from, late entry) and more sheet fields (period numbering, grace days, archived). Statements, watches, permissions and the like that get removed are recorded too, so a removed one still shows on dates before its removal.

**Things to know:**
- History is only written from now on. Changes made before this version was deployed have no records for the new kinds and fields. The test database is in memory, so the tests aren't affected.
- Refusals that fall through to the generic error say "clear the as-of date to change anything". Forms with their own message for a 403 keep it, which for some reads as a role problem (e.g. "Your role may not make that change to this claim").
- While the date is set, the Today field shows the as-of date, because the screen uses it as the sheet's today.

The tests don't check every field on screen (the settings panel, roles, delegations, patrons and watches, for example), so those are covered by the design rather than by a test.
